paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Number of tasks by language family.
model_annotation: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the number of morphosyntactic probing tasks associated with various language families, as evaluated in the context of multilingual BERT models. The vertical axis lists ten language families or groups—IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque—arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” spans from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 10, indicating the number of probing tasks per language family. The IE-Slavic family has the highest number of tasks, with a bar extending to approximately 79. IE-Romance follows with about 47 tasks, and IE-Germanic has roughly 44. Uralic is next with around 20 tasks, followed by IE-Baltic at about 17, IE-other at 15, IE-Indic at 10, Semitic at 8, Turkic at 5, and Basque at approximately 3. Each bar is uniquely colored: IE-Slavic is light blue, IE-Romance is dark blue, IE-Germanic is light green, Uralic is green, IE-Baltic is pink, IE-other is red, IE-Indic is tan, Semitic is orange, Turkic is lavender, and Basque is purple. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of Indo-European subgroups, particularly Slavic, in the probing task distribution.
